Corollary
[Curvatures of a graph] 1. ch14:14.103–14.105\group ch14-boundary-gradient For the graph of $u\in C^2(\Omega )$ in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, egin{equation} H(x_0)= rac1n \left.D_i\left( rac{D_iu}{\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}} ight) ight|_{x_0}. ag {14.103} \end{equation} Writing $ u _i=D_iu/\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}$, the squared norm of the second fundamental form is egin{equation} \mathcal G^2=\sum _{i=1}^n\kappa _i^2 =\sum _{i,j=1}^nD_i u _jD_j u _i, ag {14.104} \end{equation} and the Gauss curvature is egin{equation} K=\prod _{i=1}^n\kappa _i =\det [D_i u _j] = rac{\det D^2u}{(1+|Du|^2)^{(n+2)/2}}. ag {14.105} \end{equation} The graph is minimal precisely when $H=0$.
Proof

\sketch Apply the preceding proposition to the level function $\psi (x,x_{n+1})=x_{n+1}-u(x)$. Computing the normalized normal derivative, its trace, and its determinant gives (14.103)–(14.105).

□
